editorial.headline: Pet-Animal Retail: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership across every stated scale, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this pet-animal retail activity as PMA in Bali under the position recorded here. That conclusion matters because the national setting is otherwise unequivocal: the activity is open to foreign investment, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The Bali restriction is therefore not a softened version of the national rule, nor a question of a reduced ownership share. It is a block on PMA registration in the province.

The activity itself is straightforward but broad in the animals it encompasses. It covers the retail sale of companion animals, including cats, dogs, snakes, rabbits and monitor lizards, alongside other pet animals. The scope also records direct sales. In practical editorial terms, this is the retail end of the pet-animal trade: a business whose defining activity is selling the animals themselves to customers, rather than merely operating around the wider pet economy.

The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth gives the classification a clear national operating range, from the smallest stated business scale through to the largest. For a founder assessing foreign participation, however, the national openness is only half the answer. The national ceiling permits full foreign ownership, but location changes the registration outcome. An activity can be fully open in the national investment setting and still be unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.

Bali’s reason is explicit. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis; the record identifies the moratorium as taking effect in May 2026. For this activity, the honest Bali position is therefore categorical: full foreign ownership remains the national ceiling, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked by the province’s risk-based rule.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness permits full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-based rule blocks PMA registration for this activity.
